title: Jensen Huang on AI doomerism, open vs closed models, and going as far up the stack as needed, as low as possible
summary: Jensen rebuts AI doom predictions by pointing to failed forecasts, argues regulation should solve real problems via engineering root-cause, and explains why Nvidia runs every model and builds only what customers need. He also covers open models, supply chain foresight, and long-horizon thinking.

principles.text: Regulation should solve actual problems; root-cause incidents from an engineering perspective and institutionalize the fix.
principles.quote: regulation should solve actual problems. And so the question is what actual problems have we enjoyed,

principles.text: Safety and leadership are false choices; you can innovate, execute fast and lead safely at once.
principles.quote: You're you're able to innovate quickly. You're able to execute quickly and and uh America's able to lead and to do it safely.

principles.text: Go up the stack only as far as needed, as low as possible, then let a thousand flowers bloom.
principles.quote: Our strategy is go up as far as we need to and as low as possible.

principles.text: Build out of customer need and help everyone succeed, not to disrupt or take a slice.
principles.quote: So I do everything out of need. I'm not trying to disrupt I mean we don't wake up in the morning try to disrupt anybody.

principles.text: Think in decades: a CEO must plan the next decade and the one after, so a few years is just a click.
principles.quote: I think in decades as well you know I've been around a long time and you know for Nvidia I've got to think about what happens next decade and decade after that.

principles.text: The AI race is won by who exploits the technology best, not who invents it.
principles.quote: the race is really about who exploits the technology best.
